blocks.content: Biodiversity manifests across multiple hierarchical levels, ranging from genetic variations within a single species to complex ecological networks within entire biomes.

items: Competitive exams frequently ask to differentiate Alpha, Beta, and Gamma diversity: Alpha is local within-community diversity, Beta is species turnover between habitats, and Gamma is regional diversity.
Questions often highlight the Western Ghats having higher amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats as a standard textbook example of species richness.
Rauwolfia vomitoria (producing reserpine) in the Himalayas is a classic example used in exams to illustrate genetic diversity at the intra-species level.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Genetic diversity refers to variations in genetic information within a single species, such as variations in reserpine potency in Rauwolfia vomitoria.
Species diversity measures the variety and richness of species within a specific geographic region.
Ecological diversity encompasses variations in ecosystem structure, including deserts, rainforests, mangroves, coral reefs, and alpine meadows.
Whittaker classified spatial ecosystem diversity into Alpha (within-habitat), Beta (between-habitat), and Gamma (regional landscape) diversity.
